name: Measuring Trust and Knowledge
title: Measuring Trust and Knowledge
answer: Measuring trust and knowledge means using validated surveys to see where teachers stand on AI based tools and on ethical AI teaching before and after professional learning. It matters because it shows whether training actually changes what teachers know and do, rather than only whether it felt useful. Leaders can then design support and improve professional learning based on evidence.

sections.body: This idea is about checking professional learning with two validated instruments. One measures teachers' trust in AI based tools, including perceived benefits, concerns about transparency, anxieties, and confidence. The other, called Intelligent TPACK, measures teachers' knowledge of AI tools, their use for feedback and monitoring, subject specific tools, and ethical judgment. The problem it solves is that a training can feel good without changing knowledge or practice. Measuring before and after gives leaders a way to see growth and to keep professional learning honest.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: The text does not give grade bands for this idea, so the practice applies to a district or school across roles rather than to a particular year group. A district can use the trust instrument and Intelligent TPACK before and after professional learning. The change between the two points shows whether teachers are growing. Leaders can also combine surveys with observations and the time study from Chapter 17 to get a fuller picture. They should share results with teachers and use them to improve support.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text does not attach a separate evidence label to this idea, but it presents the approach as supported by validated instruments rather than by a single outcome study. It states that researchers developed and validated an instrument for measuring teachers' trust in AI based tools, citing Nazaretsky et al., 2022. That instrument covers perceived benefits, concerns about transparency, anxieties, and confidence. It also states that another validated instrument measures teachers' knowledge of how to use AI ethically in teaching, called Intelligent TPACK, citing Çelik, 2023. Intelligent TPACK covers knowledge of AI tools, their use for feedback and monitoring, subject specific tools, and ethical judgment.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The text sets limits on what these measures can show. Trust and knowledge surveys are not the whole picture, so surveys, observations, and the time study from Chapter 17 together give a fuller view. A training that feels good but does not change knowledge or practice is not working. Leaders should share results with teachers and use them to improve. The text does not say the instruments make decisions for a school, so the decisions about support and improvement stay with leaders.
